title: Advancing cancer detection and treatment using longitudinal routine clinical data.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: not open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no GEO/SRA/BioProject links, no Zenodo/Dryad hits on the DOI; only software RRIDs (research resource identifiers) text-mined. One web search found no public data release.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Cohort sizes (COMPASS (China Oncology Multimodal Prediction and Surveillance Study) 3.67 million people, 17.7 million visits; UK Biobank 502,665) and AUROC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) values come from the abstract and news coverage only.

a1_downloadable.note: Patient-level hospital EHR (electronic health records) and chest X-rays from Chinese hospitals; no deposited dataset found. External cohort UK Biobank needs an access application. Controlled access / not downloadable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked: no files. Cancer labels would be in hospital records, not released.

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper claims millions of people, but no accessible rows.

a6_fits_laptop.note: 17.7 million visits plus X-ray images would also exceed a laptop working set.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not checked; labels are presumably clinical diagnoses in the hospital records.

existing_models.name: Oncoformer (this paper), a multimodal transformer on EHR and chest X-ray
existing_models.score_and_split: AUROC 0.956 pan-cancer diagnosis, 0.869 one-year-ahead prediction; validated on COMPASS-Replication and UK Biobank (from abstract)

honest_claim_h3: Not applicable: the data cannot be obtained.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use routine blood tests and chest X-rays over time to predict cancer diagnosis up to a year early.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-patient histories of lab tests and chest X-rays; the paper reports 3.67 million people, but none of it is accessible (unknown verified count).
plain_idea.predict: Whether and when a person is diagnosed with cancer, and its stage, taken from hospital diagnosis and pathology records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cheap early cancer flagging from tests hospitals already run; but without the data we cannot build or test it.

ml_idea: Rejected: the only feasible route would be applying for UK Biobank access, which is an access application and outside scope.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Data availability statement: hospital EHR not deposited, UK Biobank needs application — already fails.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: patient-level Chinese hospital records are not deposited anywhere I could find, and the external cohort (UK Biobank) requires an access application; the paper is paywalled with no supplement retrievable.
